My research sits at the intersection of political behavior, public opinion, experiments, and machine learning methods for social science. Substantively, I study partisanship, polarization, anti-democratic attitudes, and political violence. Methodologically, I work on practical tools for experimental analysis, survey research, and causal inference.

Project links include articles, preprints, code, supplements, and replication materials where publicly available.

## Forthcoming

:::::: project-list
::::: project-card
### Advanced Machine Learning for Experiments in the Social Sciences

::: project-meta
Forthcoming Cambridge Element · with Jack T. Rametta & Christopher D. Hare
:::

This Element introduces machine learning methods for balance testing, attrition detection, measurement, and treatment effect estimation in experimental political science.

::: pub-actions
[Working draft](https://osf.io/preprints/osf/nm9de){.resource-link}
:::

## Publications

:::::::::::::::::::::::: project-list
::::: project-card
### Attitudes Surrounding Fairness and Competition in Sports Predict Choices to Partisan Gerrymander

::: project-meta
*Political Behavior* · with Hilary Izatt
:::

Develops a sports-based battery measuring fairness and competitiveness and links those traits to support for partisan gerrymandering.

::: pub-actions
[Article](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11109-025-10086-8){.resource-link} [Replication](https://osf.io/r2cgy/){.resource-link}
:::
:::::

::::: project-card
### Affect, Not Ideology: The Heterogeneous Effects of Partisan Cues on Policy Support

::: project-meta
*Political Behavior* · with Nicolás de la Cerda & Jack T. Rametta
:::

Uses causal forests to examine heterogeneity in partisan cue effects and shows how affective attachments shape policy responsiveness.

::: pub-actions
[Article](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11109-025-10030-w){.resource-link} [Replication](https://osf.io/mr2jq/){.resource-link}
:::
:::::

::::: project-card
### Populism and the Affective Partisan Space in Nine European Publics

::: project-meta
*Frontiers in Political Science* · with Will Horne, James Adams, & Noam Gidron
:::

Maps affective party evaluations across European publics and examines how citizens' affective ratings relate to party populism and ideology.

::: pub-actions
[Article](https://doi.org/10.3389/fpos.2022.984238){.resource-link} [Replication](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/MN4RAR){.resource-link}
:::
:::::

::::: project-card
### Assessing the Effectiveness of COVID-19 Vaccine Lotteries

::: project-meta
*PLOS One* · with Sara Kazemian, Carlos Algara, & Daniel J. Simmons
:::

Uses cross-state synthetic control methods to evaluate whether COVID-19 vaccine lottery programs increased vaccination uptake.

::: pub-actions
[Article](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0274374){.resource-link} [Replication](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/K1XX02){.resource-link}
:::
:::::

::::: project-card
### The Role of Race and Scientific Trust on Support for COVID-19 Social Distancing Measures in the United States

::: project-meta
*PLOS One* · with Sara Kazemian & Carlos Algara
:::

Examines how scientific trust shapes support for social distancing policies across racial and ethnic groups in the United States.

::: pub-actions
[Article](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0254127){.resource-link} [Replication](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/0RMZHK){.resource-link}
:::
:::::

::::: project-card
### The Interactive Effects of Scientific Knowledge and Gender on COVID-19 Social Distancing Compliance

::: project-meta
*Social Science Quarterly* · with Carlos Algara, Christopher D. Hare, & Sara Kazemian
:::

Studies the interaction between scientific knowledge and gender in explaining COVID-19 social distancing compliance.

::: pub-actions
[Article](https://doi.org/10.1111/ssqu.12894){.resource-link}
:::
:::::

::::: project-card
### The Conditional Effects of Scientific Knowledge & Gender on Support for COVID-19 Government Containment Policies in a Partisan America

::: project-meta
*Politics & Gender* · with Carlos Algara & Christopher D. Hare

Analyzes how scientific knowledge and gender condition support for COVID-19 government containment policies.

[Article](https://doi.org/10.1017/S1743923X20000458){.resource-link} [Supplementary material](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/politics-and-gender/article/conditional-effect-of-scientific-knowledge-and-gender-on-support-for-covid19-government-containment-policies-in-a-partisan-america/C4AEB27D4046433749A883941AC74809#supplementary-material){.resource-link}
